candidate.geometry: Q16 x K64, local128; four wave32s retain four query rows each for one query head
candidate.mechanism: stage one 64-row BF16 K/V plus metadata tile in LDS for reuse across 16 query rows of one query head

correctness.red: The model-scale admission test initially failed because the Q16xK64 wrapper did not exist.
correctness.green: The existing M128 preappend fixture matched both retained qrow references for every F32 output bit.

leaf_diagnostic.timing: five direct cached synthetic leaf samples per shape; retained qrow6 and candidate launched from the same process
leaf_diagnostic.reason_not_promotion_eligible: The ephemeral inline leaf command and raw samples were not preserved. These measurements are sufficient to abandon a roughly five-times-slower design but are not a retainable performance claim.

rocprof.reproduction_template: Prebuild laguna_kv_attention.so for gfx1151, then run rocprofv3 --kernel-trace around tests/test_laguna_kv_attention.py -k preappend_cached_qrow4 with HIPENGINE_REQUIRE_CACHED_BUILD=1.
rocprof.occupancy_assessment: VGPR248 makes the four-wave workgroup effectively one resident workgroup per CU.

decision.reason: A 2.75x reduction in row-group K/V requests cannot repay VGPR248, 33 KiB LDS, barriers, and staging when the tile still serves only one query head. Every tested context is about five times slower.
decision.next_premise: Co-design LC-1 with GQA reuse: one six-wave workgroup owns one global KV head and one qrow6 row group, stages K64 once, and serves all six query heads. This changes the request-amplification target from about 132x to 22x while retaining only six query rows per wave.
